_publish: Branches pre-push will let out of this machine. Empty means none, which is
I2 stated exactly: nobody pushes, and the owner of a node integrates
contributors into it. A remote runs none of these hooks, so a pushed node
branch is work no rank has integrated, somewhere the guard cannot reach.
If this repository genuinely publishes, name the branch here -- e.g.
["main"] -- and note that this file is a document, so rank 0 makes that
change deliberately and every node reads the same answer.
_globs: '*' does NOT cross '/'. '**' does. Ordinary gitignore semantics.
_never_travels: Empty by default, and think hard before filling it.
A path here is refused even when it ARRIVES BY MERGE, which aborts the whole
merge rather than skipping the path — git hooks can only allow or abort.
It is NOT needed to protect .harness/: hooks and config are read from the
document node's checkout via core.hooksPath and --git-common-dir, so a copy on
any other branch is never read and never executed. Verified by giving a code
